items.body_md:
On August 11, Stability AI (or Getty — the filing party is not identified in the docket caption) filed a second Administrative Motion under Civil Local Rule 7-11 (Dkt. 70), one day after Getty or Stability filed an Opposition or Response to the first such motion (Dkt. 69, August 10), which itself was directed at the Administrative Motion filed August 6 (Dkt. 68). All three entries are procedural in character: Civil L.R. 7-11 is the mechanism for non-noticed relief from case-management rules — page limits, scheduling adjustments, sealing requests, and similar ministerial matters — and none of the docket descriptions signals a substantive dispute touching legal rights, claims, or the September 18 fact-discovery deadline. The opposition at Dkt. 69 does establish that whatever Dkt. 68 sought, the opposing party contested it, which upgrades the pairing from purely routine to worth monitoring; if Judge Thompson or Magistrate Judge Kim rules on Dkt. 68 in a way that affects discovery scope or timing, that order will warrant coverage. The documents themselves are not publicly available through RECAP as of this writing, so the precise relief sought in Dkts. 68 and 70 remains unverified beyond their procedural classification.

The more consequential backdrop is the fact-discovery clock. The close of fact discovery is set for September 18, 2026 — five weeks out — and the administrative motion cluster arriving in August is a common signal that at least one party is pressing for some form of relief (page extensions, filing accommodations, or, less commonly, a sealing dispute) ahead of that deadline. 
Discovery disputes have been referred to Magistrate Judge Sallie Kim, per Judge Thompson's May 4, 2026 Order of Reference.
 Any motion that crosses from administrative housekeeping into a genuine discovery dispute — scope of production, privilege, or a request to extend the September 18 cutoff — would move to Magistrate Kim and become substantive-and-important. Nothing on the current docket reaches that threshold yet.

The next concrete milestone is September 18, 2026 — close of fact discovery. If either Dkt. 68 or Dkt. 70 is seeking relief that touches that deadline, an order from Judge Thompson or Magistrate Kim could accelerate or compress the remaining schedule in ways that affect Getty's ability to build its damages record ahead of any summary-judgment phase.

items.body_md:
On August 10 and 11, the claims agent docketed four additional assignments and transfers of claim (Dkts. 1192, 1195, 1196, and 1197), extending the unbroken run of secondary-market claim purchases that has characterized the docket since plan confirmation on August 5. The mechanics mirror the CRG Financial / Technical Truck And Trailer transfer (Dkt. 1165): each is a Rule 3001(e)(2) transfer other than for security, with a 20-day objection window running from mailing before the transferee is substituted without further order. Individual transfer amounts are not in the pulled document text for this batch, but at the scale of this estate — where unsecured creditor recovery turns on the outcome of more than $1 billion in antitrust litigation being pursued by plan funder Atlas Grove, __[Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/articles/2510100/harvest-sherwood-wins-ch-11-plan-approval)__ — no individual small-balance transfer changes the recovery calculus. The volume, now running across at least nine transfers since August 7 (Dkts. 1176–1179 and 1192–1197), does signal continued secondary-market appetite for Harvest Sherwood paper at confirmed-plan pricing.

Dkts. 1191 and 1198 — notices of hearing filed August 10 — remain unresolved as to which underlying motions they schedule. The most probable candidates remain the lift-stay motions filed at Dkts. 1181 and 1190 (August 7 and 10), whose full text has not been pulled; a PACER pull of either notice would confirm the connection and reveal the hearing date. Dkts. 1201–1204 are four pro hac vice admissions filed August 11, procedural-and-routine. The receipt and filing fee entry carries no independent significance.

The next concrete milestone remains trial in Adversary Proceeding 25-08002, Harvest Sherwood v. Sprouts Farmers Market, Inc., set for September 21, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. before Judge Jernigan in Dallas — confirmed by the amended notice of trial on the adversary docket, __[Epiq](https://dm.epiq11.com/case/hvs/advproc/223?debtorId=15030)__. That proceeding, in which the estate seeks approximately $41.8 million plus punitive damages on claims of fraudulent transfer, breach of contract, fraud, and unjust enrichment, is the highest-materiality near-term event for unsecured creditor recovery alongside the antitrust portfolio. Any pre-trial motion — in limine, summary judgment, or stipulation — filed in Adv. Pro. 25-08002 before September 21 will carry the highest priority for this desk.

items.body_md:
On August 11, Firy filed two additional deposition notices (Dkts. 61–62) and two affidavits (Dkts. 66–67) in Case No. 26-11217 before Judge Walrath, both filings bearing on the contested Chapter 15 recognition proceeding. The deposition notices extend Firy's witness program beyond the three already noticed August 8 — Oriel Bachar, Pinni Yaniv, and James Kong (Dkts. 53–55) — adding two further deponents whose identities are not specified in the docket entry text. That expansion signals Firy is pressing a broad factual record ahead of the recognition hearing, consistent with the strategic posture of a creditor seeking to challenge the foreign proceeding's eligibility or the scope of the temporary injunction Judge Walrath granted August 9.

The two affidavits (Dkts. 66–67) are the more consequential August 11 filings. In a contested Chapter 15 recognition proceeding, sworn affidavits typically function as evidentiary support for a party's position on recognition eligibility, the debtor's center-of-main-interests, or the terms under which a temporary injunction should be continued or dissolved. The docket record does not specify which party submitted them or what propositions they address; that detail will control how they bear on Firy's recovery posture. If they are Papaya-side submissions, they likely shore up the COMI analysis or the Israeli fund structure. If Firy-side, they are likely directed at contesting one of those same points. Until the documents themselves are reviewed, the filing cannot be assigned a directional weight — but their timing, three affidavits-and-depositions days into a contested proceeding with no recognition hearing date yet set, confirms both sides are building a litigation record at pace.

Three further pro hac vice motions were filed August 10 (Dkts. 58–60), continuing the counsel-buildout on the Firy side that the Latham & Watkins admissions (Dkts. 56–57, approving Ardeljan and Quartarolo) completed the same day. Dkts. 63–65, three additional pro hac vice motions filed August 11, deepen that roster further. No recognition hearing date appears on the docket as of this briefing; that date, once set, will be the controlling deadline against which both sides' deposition and affidavit schedules are paced.

items.body_md:
On August 11, RNDC's docket recorded Dkts. 160–174 — five pro hac vice orders (Dkts. 163–167), additional pro hac vice appearances (Dkts. 160, 169, 170, 171), notices of appearance and request for notice (Dkts. 162, 168, 173), affidavits (Dkts. 161, 172), and a notice (Dkt. 174) — all procedural and routine, with no bearing on recovery or timing.

The substantive picture remains unchanged. The lift-stay motion at Dkt. 146, filed August 7, has drawn no docketed response. The response deadline falls on or about August 22 under S.D. Tex. Bankruptcy Local Rule 4001-1 — two days before the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24. No amended plan, plan supplement, or conditional approval order on the Disclosure Statement (Dkt. 118, filed August 4) has appeared on the docket. Until Judge Lopez enters a conditional approval order, the solicitation and voting timeline cannot be set, and no class of creditors can be formally canvassed.

The August 24 second-day hearing remains the next concrete milestone. Unless Dkt. 146 is resolved by stipulated order before that date, the lift-stay motion arrives before Judge Lopez in one of three postures: contested (if a timely response is filed by August 22), resolved by agreed order, or unopposed and subject to grant. A granted motion removes estate property from the distributable pool before any 363 sale has closed — compounding the structural gap between RNDC's disclosed asset range of $500 million to $1 billion and its $1 billion to $10 billion in liabilities, and bearing directly on recoveries for the approximately 100,000 unsecured creditors owed more than $400 million per __[The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2026/08/rndc-court-filings-reveal-scale-of-distributors-financial-collapse/)__. The growing volume of pro hac vice admissions — now spanning Dkts. 150–155, 160, 163–167, 169–171 across a six-day window — signals that multiple constituencies are mobilizing counsel, consistent with an adversarial posture heading into the second-day hearing, though no formal objections to any pending motion have yet appeared on the docket.
